item.content:encoded:
Are you a recent PhD graduate in economics or a related field looking to build a career as an international economist? The International Monetary Fund (IMF) Economist Program (EP) offers talented economists the opportunity to work on real-world economic policy challenges and contribute to issues affecting the IMF’s 191 member countries.

IMF Economist Program

The International Monetary Fund’s Economist Program (EP) is the IMF’s flagship entry program for PhD economists.

Designed for recent PhD graduates and economists completing their doctoral studies, the EP provides an accelerated introduction to the IMF’s policy, analytical, and operational work. Through structured rotational assignments and direct engagement with economic policy issues, the program serves as a foundation for a long-term career as an IMF economist.

The EP is not a trainee program. Participants join the IMF as economists and contribute from the outset to country work, research, policy development, and capacity development activities.

The three-year rotational program gives economists hands-on experience across the IMF’s work, from country missions and surveillance to policy analysis and research.

About the International Monetary Fund

The IMF is a global institution with 191 member countries. Its mission is to promote international monetary cooperation, financial stability, sustainable economic growth, and poverty reduction.

Economists at the IMF work across a wide range of policy areas including:

  • Macroeconomic surveillance
  • Fiscal policy
  • Monetary and exchange rate policy
  • Financial sector analysis
  • External sector assessment
  • Debt sustainability
  • Capacity development
  • Policy research

Working at the IMF provides a unique opportunity to apply economic expertise in a multinational environment, engaging directly with member country authorities, central banks, ministries of finance, international institutions, and policymakers around the world.

IMF Economist Program Structure

The Economist Program is a three-year rotational program based at IMF Headquarters in Washington, D.C.

Participants complete two departmental assignments designed to provide broad exposure to the IMF’s work and develop a strong foundation in macroeconomic policy and surveillance.

Program Detail Information
Duration 3 years
Structure Two departmental assignments
Location Washington, D.C.
Eligibility Recent PhD or within one year of completion
Application opens September
Application closes December
Start September of the following year
Cohort size Approximately 20–30 per year
Career path Long-term IMF economist career
Program type Rotational economist entry program

What Do IMF Economist Program Participants Do?

During the program, participants rotate through two departmental assignments, joining economic teams working in regional and country-specific surveillance as well as on fiscal, monetary, balance of payments, debt, and related issues.

Country Work and IMF Missions

EP economists contribute to IMF Article IV consultations and country programs, analyzing economic developments and helping advise member countries.

Country assignments may involve evaluating economic developments, assessing risks and vulnerabilities, contributing to policy recommendations, and participating in country teams.

Policy Analysis

Participants contribute to IMF policy advice on fiscal, monetary, financial, debt, and external sector issues, supporting IMF advice to member countries.

Research

EP economists contribute to research and analytical work that can inform IMF policy frameworks, analytical methods, flagship publications, and policy decisions.

Research assignments often involve applying advanced economic methods to practical policy questions.

Capacity Development and Teaching

Participants may support training, technical assistance, and knowledge-sharing activities that help member countries strengthen institutions and policymaking capacity.

Who Can Apply for the IMF Economist Program?

The Economist Program is intended for economists ready to apply their doctoral research and analytical training to real-world policy challenges.

Academic Qualifications

Applicants should be:

  • Recent PhD graduates or within one year of completing a PhD in economics or a related field.
  • From relevant fields such as macroeconomics, monetary economics, international economics, public finance, financial economics, econometrics, and related disciplines.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must:

  • Be a national of one of the IMF’s member countries.
  • Be under age 34 at the time of entry into the Economist Program.

Eligible applicants can be nationals of any of the IMF’s 191 member countries: Afghanistan, Albania, Algeria, Andorra, Angola, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Armenia, Australia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Ghana, Greece, Grenada, Guatemala, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Hungary, Iceland, India, Indonesia, Iran, Iraq, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Jamaica, Japan, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

Core Skills and Competencies

Candidates should demonstrate:

  • Strong quantitative and analytical capabilities
  • Excellent research skills and policy judgment
  • Ability to apply economic theory to policy problems
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Strong presentation, interpersonal, and communication skills
  • Ability to explain complex economic issues clearly and logically

Additional IMF languages are an asset.

IMF Economist Program Application Cycle

The Economist Program follows a structured annual recruitment cycle, so prospective applicants should plan ahead.

September – Applications Open

Applications open in September, with on-campus and online/virtual preliminary interviews beginning during this period.

December – Applications Close

The application window typically closes in December.

December–January – Panel Interviews and Assessments

Candidates who progress through the recruitment process participate in panel interviews and assessments, including activities held at IMF Headquarters.

February – Offers

Successful candidates receive offers in February.

September – Program Begins

The incoming Economist Program cohort begins in September.

IMF Economist Program Selection Process

Throughout the selection process, the IMF assesses candidates’ analytical skills, judgment, communication abilities, and ability to apply economic thinking to real-world challenges.

Step 1: Preliminary Interview

Shortlisted candidates participate in a 30–40 minute preliminary interview.

The interview includes a high-level overview of the candidate’s research and discussion of economic topics related to the IMF’s work, as well as interpersonal and communication skills.

Step 2: Research Paper, Transcript and References

Candidates may be asked to submit:

  • Their most recent PhD university transcript
  • Three academic references
  • A research paper of publishable standard or one or two dissertation chapters

References cannot be from current IMF staff members.

Step 3: Panel Interview and Written Assessment

Selected candidates participate in a panel interview with senior IMF economists and a Human Resources officer.

Candidates also complete a 90-minute written assessment designed to evaluate written communication skills and the ability to write under time constraints.

Step 4: Final Selection and Offer

Following the panel interviews and assessments, candidates are referred for final review. The highest weighting is given to the panel interview and research paper review.

Why Join the IMF Economist Program?

Real Work From Day One

The EP is not a trainee program. Participants assume substantive responsibilities from the beginning of their assignments.

Broad Exposure

The rotation structure provides experience across departments, policy areas, countries, and regions.

Intellectual Rigor

EP economists work alongside experienced IMF economists on complex challenges affecting member countries and the global economy.

International Policy Experience

The program provides opportunities to work on economic issues affecting countries around the world, including through country missions, surveillance, policy analysis and research.

Long-Term Career Development

The program is designed to prepare economists for long-term careers at the IMF.

IMF Economist Program Alumni

After completing their rotations, EP alumni go on to build careers across the IMF and beyond, continuing to work on global economic challenges across areas such as surveillance, research, and policy.

The IMF highlights the experience of its alumni, including the opportunity to apply research to economic policy questions affecting countries around the world and to broaden economists’ perspectives and skills through the program’s departmental rotations.

The program therefore provides not only initial exposure to the IMF but also a foundation for continued professional development as an economist.

IMF Economist Program – Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Economist Program a trainee program?

No. EP participants are hired as economists and take on substantive responsibilities from the beginning of their assignments.

How long is the program?

The program lasts three years and includes two departmental assignments.

When do IMF Economist Program applications open?

Applications typically open in September.

When does the application close?

The current recruitment cycle indicates that applications close in December.

Are preliminary interviews conducted online?

Yes. Preliminary interviews may begin in September and can take place on campus or online/virtually.

What materials may be requested after the preliminary interview?

Candidates may be asked to provide a PhD transcript, three academic references, and a research paper or dissertation chapters.

What assessments are included?

The process may include a preliminary interview, research paper review, panel interview, and written assessment.

When are offers made?

Offers are typically made in February.

When does the IMF Economist Program start?

The incoming class starts at the IMF in September.

What happens after the program?

The EP is designed as a pathway to a long-term career as an IMF economist.

IMF Economist Program Career Opportunities

The program is designed to develop economists who can contribute to the IMF’s policy, analytical, and operational work across a wide range of member country issues.

EP economists may pursue long-term careers across the IMF in areas such as:

  • Country and regional surveillance
  • Fiscal affairs
  • Monetary and capital markets
  • Research
  • Strategy and policy development
  • Capacity development and technical assistance

How to Apply for the IMF Economist Program

Are you ready to launch your career as an IMF economist? Apply Now for the Economist Program

The Economist Program is an opportunity for recent PhD economists to apply their research, quantitative skills and economic expertise to real-world policy challenges affecting the global economy.

Learn more and view current opportunities:
IMF Careers

Official IMF Economist Program:
International Monetary Fund – Economist Program

Apply Now for the Economist Program

item.content:encoded:
The Solon Fellowship Program, organized by Elected Officials to Protect America (EOPA), is offering an opportunity for motivated young professionals to gain practical experience in climate policy, environmental protection, public leadership, communications, research, fundraising, project management, and civic engagement.

The fellowship is designed for individuals who want to contribute to projects with national and international policy relevance while working alongside current and former elected officials, environmental advocates, veterans, frontline leaders, and other professionals committed to protecting the environment and strengthening democratic institutions.

Applications are currently being accepted for the Summer Cohort ’26.

The program provides fellows with an opportunity to participate in meaningful organizational projects, receive specialized professional training, develop relationships with elected officials and policy leaders, and potentially advance into more senior fellowship positions.

Importantly, the fellowship can be completed remotely, from EOPA’s offices in Rockland, Maine or Washington, DC, or internationally, making it potentially attractive to qualified applicants outside the United States.

About Elected Officials to Protect America

Elected Officials to Protect America (EOPA) is described as a nonpartisan network of current and former elected officials focused on protecting land, water, democracy, and environmental justice.

The organization works at the intersection of:

  • Climate policy
  • Environmental protection
  • Public leadership
  • Democratic governance
  • Environmental justice
  • Energy security
  • Climate finance
  • Clean transportation
  • Land and water conservation
  • Public communication
  • Policy advocacy

EOPA’s approach combines policy mobilization, education and training, and media and storytelling.

According to the fellowship information, the organization has organized hundreds of elected officials across all 50 U.S. states and has also worked internationally.

Its activities include supporting policy initiatives, educating lawmakers and civic leaders, producing media campaigns and documentaries, and creating opportunities for elected officials and emerging professionals to develop leadership and policy skills.

What Makes the Solon Fellowship Different?

The Solon Fellowship is not simply structured as a conventional work-placement program.

Instead, fellows are expected to become involved in a range of organizational activities and may have opportunities to contribute to projects involving research, policy, communications, partnerships, fundraising, media production, and project management.

The fellowship therefore provides exposure to multiple areas of public-interest work.

For individuals interested in environmental governance, climate policy, international development, public administration, political communication, nonprofit management, sustainability, urban governance, advocacy, or public leadership, the program can provide a multidisciplinary professional experience.

Areas of Work and Strategic Focus

EOPA identifies three major areas through which it advances its mission.

1. Policy and Mobilizing

One major component of EOPA’s work involves mobilizing elected officials and supporting policy initiatives.

The organization works with lawmakers, including veterans and elected officials representing frontline communities, through leadership councils and specialized task forces.

Fellows may therefore gain exposure to activities involving:

  • Policy research
  • Legislative advocacy
  • Public policy communication
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Political outreach
  • Environmental policy
  • Climate policy
  • Energy security
  • Clean transportation
  • Climate finance
  • Land and water conservation
  • Nature-based solutions
  • International policy initiatives

The organization emphasizes peer-to-peer education, based on the idea that elected officials can be particularly effective in educating and influencing fellow lawmakers.

EOPA states that its policy work has included initiatives ranging from international energy-security proposals and United Nations climate negotiations to national and state-level environmental policies.

2. Education and Training

The second major area is education and professional development.

EOPA works jointly with the University of San Francisco to operate a Public Leadership Certificate designed to strengthen the leadership and policy capabilities of lawmakers and civic leaders.

The program covers areas including:

  • Emotional intelligence
  • Leadership
  • Management
  • Public speaking
  • Body language
  • Value-based communications
  • Legislative procedures
  • Cybersecurity
  • Empathy
  • Fundraising

Participants also have opportunities to interact with elected officials who have played significant roles in public policy.

The fellowship provides an opportunity for fellows to potentially participate in this leadership certificate program.

EOPA states that more than 200 leaders from around the world apply for the Public Leadership Certificate, with approximately 37 participants accepted on average.

This makes access to the certificate a potentially significant professional-development benefit for successful fellows.

3. Media and Storytelling

EOPA also places significant emphasis on communication, journalism, storytelling, and visual media.

The organization has an in-house film production arm that develops media intended to educate lawmakers, journalists, and members of the public.

Its work has included:

  • Digital advertisements
  • Short documentaries
  • Environmental campaigns
  • Water-security storytelling
  • Policy communication
  • Video production
  • Print articles
  • Letters
  • Op-eds
  • Policy solutions

The organization also operates ProtectEarth.News, a newsmagazine intended to bring together videos, articles, policy solutions, letters, and opinion pieces.

For fellows interested in strategic communications, journalism, public relations, digital media, filmmaking, storytelling, advocacy communications, or political communication, this area could provide particularly relevant experience.

Who Is the Fellowship Looking For?

The Solon Fellowship is intended for motivated and dedicated young professionals who are prepared to support and potentially lead different types of organizational projects and programs.

The opportunity specifically highlights candidates interested in areas such as:

  • Research
  • Partnerships
  • Fundraising
  • Video editing
  • Video production
  • Op-ed writing
  • Data management
  • Project management
  • Policy-related work
  • Communications
  • Public leadership
  • Environmental advocacy

Applicants do not necessarily need to specialize in only one of these areas.

The fellowship appears particularly suitable for people who are adaptable and interested in working across different functions within a mission-driven organization.

Fellowship Responsibilities and Potential Areas of Contribution

Because EOPA works across policy, communications, education, and mobilization, fellows may have opportunities to contribute to different projects depending on their skills and the organization’s needs.

Potential areas include:

Research and policy

Fellows may contribute to research activities supporting environmental and public policy initiatives.

This could include gathering information, analyzing policy issues, preparing briefing materials, supporting advocacy initiatives, or contributing to written policy products.

Partnerships

Fellows interested in stakeholder engagement may contribute to partnership development and relationship-building activities.

This could involve working with elected officials, organizations, civic leaders, environmental groups, and other stakeholders.

Fundraising

The program also exposes fellows to nonprofit and political fundraising.

This includes learning how fundraising messages can be developed around shared values and how organizations can build stronger relationships with potential funders.

Communications

Fellows may support communications activities such as:

  • Writing
  • Editing
  • Story development
  • Public messaging
  • Campaign communication
  • Media materials
  • Value-based communications

Video production

Candidates with media-production skills may have opportunities to contribute to video editing and production.

Op-ed writing

The organization’s emphasis on policy communication creates opportunities for fellows interested in opinion writing, public commentary, and policy storytelling.

Data and project management

Candidates with analytical and organizational skills can potentially contribute to data-management and project-management activities.

Fellowship Duration and Working Hours

The fellowship is structured as a four-month program.

Fellows can work between:

20 and 40 hours per week

This flexible structure can make the program suitable for individuals who need to balance professional development with other academic, professional, or personal commitments.

The organization also indicates that the fellowship may be extended beyond the initial four-month period.

Remote and International Work Options

One of the notable features of the Solon Fellowship is its flexible location arrangement.

The fellowship can be undertaken:

  • Online/remotely
  • At EOPA’s office in Rockland, Maine
  • At its Washington, DC location
  • Internationally

The availability of international participation is particularly important for applicants who are not based in the United States.

However, applicants should carefully review the application form and any subsequent communication from EOPA to confirm whether particular positions have location-specific requirements.

Fellowship Stipend

Selected fellows may receive a $1,000 stipend for the fellowship period, with the amount described as being commensurate with experience.

It is important to distinguish this from a salary or fully funded employment package.

The opportunity describes the payment specifically as a stipend for the fellowship period.

Applicants should therefore review the fellowship’s terms carefully to understand the payment structure and any conditions attached to it.

APPLY ONLINE HERE: Solon Fellowship Application

If the form is not accessible, please email talent@eopa.org

Professional Development Opportunities

The Solon Fellowship places considerable emphasis on professional development.

Fellows receive specialized training covering areas that can be useful well beyond environmental advocacy.

The training includes:

  1. Emotional Intelligence and Public Leadership
  2. Value-Based Communications
  3. Empathy-Based Fundraising
  4. Job-specific mentorship and training

These components are intended to help fellows develop both technical and interpersonal capabilities.

Emotional Intelligence and Public Leadership Training

The emotional intelligence component focuses on improving participants’ ability to:

  • Understand other people’s perspectives
  • Empathize with others
  • Listen accurately
  • Communicate authentically
  • Work effectively with teams
  • Improve team performance
  • Encourage creativity
  • Develop stronger leadership practices

These skills can be particularly valuable for professionals working in public administration, government, nonprofit organizations, advocacy, development, communications, and community engagement.

Value-Based Communications Training

The fellowship also provides training in value-based communication.

The underlying principle is that effective public communication requires more than simply providing information.

Participants learn about:

  • Framing
  • Targeting
  • Narrative development
  • Media campaigns
  • Storytelling
  • Emotional connection
  • Public communication
  • Campaign messaging

Fellows are expected to apply the concepts to real-world activities, including events, press conferences, and media campaigns.

This makes the training potentially valuable for people pursuing careers in strategic communication, public relations, political communication, environmental advocacy, development communication, or journalism.

Empathy-Based Fundraising Training

Another specialized component focuses on fundraising.

Participants are introduced to fundraising approaches used by political campaigns and nonprofit organizations.

The training explores how organizations can build relationships with funders by connecting fundraising appeals to shared values and demonstrating empathy.

Topics include:

  • Fundraising fundamentals
  • Political campaign fundraising
  • Nonprofit fundraising
  • Fundraising appeals
  • Donor engagement
  • Values-based communication
  • Relationship building
  • Advanced fundraising strategies

This can be particularly useful for professionals interested in nonprofit management, development organizations, civil society, political campaigns, or social-impact organizations.

Public Leadership Certificate Opportunity

One of the fellowship’s potentially significant benefits is the opportunity to attend EOPA’s Public Leadership Certificate.

According to the program information, more than 200 leaders from around the world apply for the certificate, while approximately 37 are accepted on average.

The certificate is designed to develop practical capabilities in leadership, communication, management, public policy, and related areas.

Participation can therefore provide fellows with an additional professional-development experience beyond their day-to-day fellowship responsibilities.

Networking Opportunities

Successful fellows can also expand their professional network through interaction with:

  • Current and former elected officials
  • State and local leaders
  • Environmental policy advocates
  • Other fellows
  • Alumni
  • Civic leaders
  • Public-policy professionals
  • EOPA staff and partners

The fellowship specifically highlights the opportunity to join its community of current fellows and alumni.

For early-career professionals, this network can potentially support future collaborations, employment opportunities, policy initiatives, and professional development.

Direct Exposure to Public Policy

Another major advantage is the opportunity to work on programs that EOPA describes as having national and international policy impacts.

Rather than limiting fellows to theoretical learning, the program is structured around practical projects.

Fellows can potentially observe how policy ideas are:

  1. Researched
  2. Developed
  3. Communicated
  4. Mobilized
  5. Presented to decision-makers
  6. Connected with broader public campaigns

This practical orientation may be particularly valuable for applicants pursuing careers in government, policy research, environmental governance, development, advocacy, or international affairs.

Career Advancement Opportunities

The fellowship can also function as a pathway into more senior roles within the organization.

EOPA states that fellows may have opportunities to advance into:

  • Senior Fellow positions
  • Executive Fellow positions

The organization also indicates that it traditionally hires from its existing pool of fellows and alumni.

This means that the fellowship may provide more than short-term experience; strong performance can potentially create opportunities for continued involvement with the organization.

Click here for more information on Solon Fellowship

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Emerging Professionals

The Solon Fellowship may be particularly valuable for professionals who want to combine career development with public-interest work.

The program brings together several fields that are increasingly interconnected in contemporary governance.

These include:

Climate and environmental governance

Climate change requires professionals who understand policy, institutions, communication, financing, infrastructure, and community engagement.

Public leadership

The opportunity provides exposure to elected officials and public leaders, offering insight into how policy is communicated and implemented.

Nonprofit management

The fundraising, partnership, project-management, and communications components can help fellows understand how mission-driven organizations operate.

Policy communication

The emphasis on storytelling and value-based communication can strengthen a fellow’s ability to communicate complex policy issues to wider audiences.

International engagement

The organization’s stated international work and international working option can provide exposure beyond conventional U.S.-focused professional environments.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The fellowship may be particularly relevant to applicants with backgrounds or interests in:

  • Public policy
  • Political science
  • Environmental studies
  • Climate change
  • Urban governance
  • Urban planning
  • Development studies
  • International development
  • Public administration
  • Sustainability
  • Environmental management
  • Communications
  • Journalism
  • Media
  • Data analysis
  • Project management
  • Nonprofit management
  • Fundraising
  • Advocacy
  • Community development
  • Public leadership

Applicants who can demonstrate initiative, strong communication skills, research ability, adaptability, and a commitment to public-interest work may be especially well positioned.

Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the information provided.

The opportunity is described as currently accepting applications for the Summer Cohort ’26, so prospective applicants should verify the current status directly through the official application page rather than assuming that applications will remain open indefinitely.

Click here for more global fellowship programs 

Conclusion

The Solon Fellowship Program offers a multidisciplinary professional-development opportunity for young professionals interested in climate action, environmental policy, public leadership, communications, advocacy, research, nonprofit management, and policy implementation.

Its combination of practical project experience, specialized training, exposure to elected officials, networking, leadership development, and potential career progression makes it particularly relevant to individuals seeking to build careers at the intersection of public policy, environmental sustainability, governance, communications, and social impact.

The program is also notable for its flexible working arrangements, with opportunities to work remotely, from EOPA’s U.S. offices, or internationally. The four-month fellowship requires between 20 and 40 hours per week, and selected fellows may receive a $1,000 stipend.

For professionals who want to move beyond academic knowledge and gain practical experience contributing to real-world policy, advocacy, communications, and environmental initiatives, the Solon Fellowship could provide a valuable platform for developing both technical and leadership capabilities.

Applications for the Summer Cohort ’26 are currently being accepted. Since no specific closing date is provided in the announcement, interested applicants should apply as soon as possible and verify the current application status through EOPA’s official application channel.

item.content:encoded:
Are you a journalist, communications professional, content creator, influencer, media presenter, or communications specialist based in Sub-Saharan Africa?

The Connect & Create Relay Scheme 2026 is offering an opportunity for young communications professionals to strengthen their skills, gain practical experience, and develop their professional networks while contributing to cultural projects in their own countries.

The programme is part of Connect & Create – Strengthening Cultural Ties Between Africa and Europe, an initiative focused on supporting cultural cooperation, professional development, mobility, networking, and sustainable connections between Sub-Saharan Africa and Europe.

The Relay Scheme is specifically designed for early-career communications professionals with two to five years of professional experience in communications, journalism, media, or content creation.

Selected participants will work directly with Creative Tandem projects in their respective countries while receiving structured professional development through training and individual mentoring.

The programme will support 16 participants residing in 12 participating Sub-Saharan African countries and will run for approximately 11 months.

What Is the Connect & Create Relay Scheme?

The Connect & Create Relay Scheme is a professional development programme for young communications professionals working across the cultural and creative sectors.

It forms part of the wider Connect & Create programme, which is the Sub-Saharan Africa component of the Africa–Europe Partnerships for Culture programme.

Connect & Create is funded by the European Union and led by the Goethe-Institut and Expertise France, in partnership with the Institut français. The Relay Scheme itself is coordinated by Imago Médias.

The wider Connect & Create initiative aims to strengthen cultural relationships between Sub-Saharan Africa and the European Union through professional exchanges, capacity building, artistic cooperation, mobility, networking, and support for cultural professionals.

The Relay Scheme focuses specifically on the communications side of this work.

Participants will combine practical experience with structured learning, allowing them to contribute to cultural projects while strengthening their own professional capabilities.

What Does the Relay Scheme Offer?

The programme combines several forms of professional development.

Participants will have the opportunity to:

  • Work directly with a Creative Tandem project in their country.
  • Gain practical experience in cultural communications.
  • Participate in structured professional training.
  • Receive individual mentoring.
  • Develop their storytelling skills.
  • Strengthen their social media communication skills.
  • Improve editorial planning and strategy.
  • Gain experience in press and media relations.
  • Develop their cultural reporting capabilities.
  • Build connections with communications professionals from other participating African countries.
  • Become part of the wider Connect & Create professional ecosystem.
  • Receive a training certificate.
  • Receive an allowance for communication activities carried out for the supported project.

The official programme description confirms that participants will complete 10 themed training sessions covering areas such as storytelling, social media, editorial strategy, and press relations, alongside one-to-one mentoring.

Who Is the Programme Designed For?

The Connect & Create Relay Scheme is aimed at young communications professionals who already have professional experience but are still developing their careers.

Eligible professional profiles include:

  • Journalists
  • Communications professionals
  • Communications specialists
  • Content creators
  • Influencers
  • Media hosts
  • Media presenters

Applicants should have between two and five years of professional experience in communications, journalism, media, or content creation.

The programme is particularly relevant to professionals who have already built some experience and an audience but want to strengthen their professional skills through practical cultural communications work.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be over 18 years old.

This means applicants must have reached adulthood by the time of application.

The programme is intended for young professionals, but the official eligibility requirement specifically establishes that applicants must be over 18 rather than giving a separate upper age limit.

Professional Experience Requirement

Applicants must have two to five years of professional experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Communications
  • Journalism
  • Media
  • Content creation

This requirement means the programme is not intended solely for people who are completely new to communications.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate previous professional work and provide evidence through their CV and portfolio.

Interest in Culture and the Creative Industries

Applicants should have an interest in:

  • Performing arts
  • Music
  • Cultural communication
  • Cultural reporting
  • Creative industries
  • Arts and culture-related projects

The programme connects communications professionals with Creative Tandem projects, meaning applicants should be interested in communicating cultural and creative work to audiences.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to professionals who enjoy storytelling, cultural journalism, digital media, social media, arts communication, and creative-sector content.

Audience and Local Presence

Applicants should have an active audience and demonstrate a meaningful local presence.

This can be demonstrated through:

  • Social media platforms
  • Media platforms
  • Community networks
  • Professional networks
  • Other relevant communication channels

The official programme states that particular attention will be paid to applicants’ experience, motivation, local roots, and audience reach.

This means applicants should not only demonstrate professional experience but should also show that they understand and engage with their local communities and audiences.

Language Requirement

Applicants must be proficient in either:

  • English, or
  • French

Applications can be submitted in either English or French.

The CV and portfolio materials should therefore be prepared in one of the accepted languages where required.

Eligible Countries

The Connect & Create Relay Scheme is open to applicants residing in one of 12 participating countries.

These countries are:

  1. South Africa
  2. Benin
  3. Cameroon
  4. Ghana
  5. Guinea
  6. Kenya
  7. Mali
  8. Mozambique
  9. Uganda
  10. Republic of the Congo
  11. Rwanda
  12. Senegal

Applicants must reside in one of these countries to be eligible for the Relay Scheme.

Applicants living in other African countries should not assume that they are eligible simply because the programme is generally focused on Sub-Saharan Africa. The Relay Scheme specifically identifies these 12 participating countries.

What Will Participants Do?

Participants will work directly with a Creative Tandem project in their own country.

The practical component allows participants to apply their communications skills to real cultural projects rather than learning only through theoretical training.

Depending on the project and participant’s role, activities may involve areas such as:

Storytelling

Participants can use storytelling techniques to communicate the ideas, people, activities, and impact associated with cultural projects.

Effective storytelling can help audiences understand why a cultural project matters and encourage greater engagement.

Social Media

Participants will develop experience communicating cultural projects through social media.

This can include developing content, engaging audiences, supporting campaigns, and using appropriate platforms to increase visibility.

Editorial Planning

Editorial strategy is another important component of the programme.

Participants can develop skills in planning content, identifying relevant themes, structuring communications activities, and maintaining consistent messaging.

Media Relations

Participants can gain practical exposure to communicating with media outlets and journalists.

This can include developing media-facing content and supporting efforts to generate media attention for cultural projects.

Cultural Reporting

The programme also provides an opportunity to develop experience in cultural reporting and communications.

This can involve communicating stories related to performing arts, music, cultural activities, creative practitioners, and related projects.

Training Programme

The professional development component includes 10 themed training sessions.

The official programme identifies areas including:

  • Storytelling
  • Social media
  • Editorial strategy
  • Press relations

The sessions are designed to strengthen participants’ practical communications capabilities while they work on their assigned cultural projects.

The training component allows participants to complement their existing professional experience with structured learning.

Individual Mentoring

Participants will also receive one-to-one mentoring.

Individual mentoring can provide a more personalized professional development experience, allowing participants to receive guidance relevant to their own career development and communications work.

Combined with the group training sessions and practical project experience, the mentoring component creates a multi-dimensional professional development structure.

Professional Network

Another important benefit of the programme is access to a professional network.

Participants will have opportunities to connect with communications professionals from the participating African countries as well as the broader Connect & Create ecosystem.

This can help participants:

  • Exchange ideas.
  • Learn from professionals in other countries.
  • Discover different approaches to cultural communications.
  • Build professional relationships.
  • Explore potential future collaborations.
  • Gain exposure to regional cultural and creative networks.

For early-career communications professionals, these connections can become an important part of long-term professional development.

Training Certificate

Participants will receive a training certificate as part of the programme.

A certificate can provide formal documentation of participation in the professional development programme and can be included in future professional portfolios, CVs, and applications where appropriate.

Financial Support

The programme provides an allowance for communication activities carried out for the supported project.

The information provided does not specify a single fixed amount for the allowance.

Applicants should therefore consult the official guidelines for the precise financial arrangements, eligible activities, and any applicable conditions.

Programme Duration

The Relay Scheme provides approximately 11 months of support.

According to the official timeline, the programme is expected to begin in late January or early February 2027.

This extended period allows participants to combine practical project work with training, mentoring, and professional networking.

Application Timeline

Applicants should pay close attention to the programme timeline.

Applications Open

15 September 2026

Application Deadline

13 October 2026

Shortlisting

14 October to 3 November 2026

During this period, applications will be reviewed and candidates will be shortlisted.

Creative Tandem Project Proposal

5 to 19 November 2026

Shortlisted candidates will be asked to submit a proposal for a Creative Tandem project.

Announcement of the 16 Connect & Create Hubs

7 December 2026

The selected hubs will be announced.

Programme Start

Late January or early February 2027

The professional development programme is expected to begin around this period.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit an online application.

The application should include:

1. Online Application Form

Applicants must complete the designated online application form.

2. Short CV

Applicants must provide a short CV in either English or French.

The CV should clearly demonstrate relevant professional experience in communications, journalism, media, or content creation.

3. Portfolio

Applicants must provide a portfolio containing two to three examples of previous work.

The portfolio is important because it allows applicants to demonstrate their practical communications capabilities rather than relying solely on descriptions in their CV.

Examples could include relevant work such as:

  • Published articles
  • Journalism work
  • Social media campaigns
  • Digital content
  • Cultural reporting
  • Video or multimedia content
  • Editorial projects
  • Communications campaigns
  • Media work
  • Other professional communications outputs

Applicants should choose examples that best demonstrate their communication skills and experience.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should approach the application as an opportunity to demonstrate both professional experience and a clear interest in cultural communications.

Demonstrate Relevant Experience

Clearly explain your professional experience over the last two to five years.

Focus on work that demonstrates communications, journalism, media, content creation, storytelling, or audience engagement.

Make Your Portfolio Relevant

Do not simply submit random examples of previous work.

Choose two or three pieces that demonstrate your strongest and most relevant communications abilities.

Where possible, select work that demonstrates:

  • Storytelling
  • Audience engagement
  • Editorial judgment
  • Social media communication
  • Cultural or community reporting
  • Media relations
  • Creative content production

Demonstrate Local Understanding

Because the programme emphasizes local roots and working with Creative Tandem projects in participants’ countries, applicants should demonstrate their understanding of their local audience and cultural environment.

Explain Your Motivation

Applicants should clearly communicate why they are interested in cultural communications and how participation in the programme could contribute to their professional development.

Highlight Audience Reach

If you have an established audience through social media, media platforms, websites, community networks, or other channels, provide relevant evidence.

Audience reach should be presented accurately and, where possible, supported with measurable information.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly relevant to professionals who want to combine communications with culture and the creative industries.

Potential applicants include:

  • Early-career journalists
  • Digital communications professionals
  • Social media professionals
  • Content creators
  • Cultural journalists
  • Media presenters
  • Influencers
  • Storytellers
  • Communications specialists
  • Creative-sector communicators

The strongest fit will generally be professionals who can demonstrate relevant experience, an active audience, local connections, and a genuine interest in performing arts, music, and cultural industries.

About Connect & Create

The Relay Scheme forms part of the broader Connect & Create – Strengthening Cultural Ties Between Africa and Europe programme.

Connect & Create is the Sub-Saharan Africa component of the Africa–Europe Partnerships for Culture programme, which is funded by the European Union.

The wider initiative aims to strengthen cultural ties between Sub-Saharan Africa and the European Union through cooperation, inclusion, sustainability, professional development, and cultural exchange.

The programme includes several support areas for professionals in performing arts and music, including:

  • Connect & Create Relay Scheme
  • Mentoring Scheme
  • Circulation of Performing Arts and Music
  • Professional Mobility
  • Creative Tandems

The Relay Scheme specifically focuses on communications professionals.

Focus on Young Professionals

Connect & Create places particular emphasis on younger generations and emerging cultural scenes.

The wider programme recognizes the importance of young people’s creativity, energy, and leadership in shaping future Africa–Europe cultural relationships.

The programme also highlights priorities including:

  • Supporting younger generations
  • Promoting emerging cultural scenes
  • Originality
  • Connection to local context
  • Sustainable collaboration
  • Environmentally responsible approaches
  • Inclusion
  • Accessibility

Key Details at a Glance

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Connect & Create Relay Scheme 2026 is:

13 October 2026

Applications must be submitted through the official online application process.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to prepare their CV and portfolio, particularly because the portfolio is an important part of the application.

The official Institut français page confirms the application opening date of 15 September 2026 and the deadline of 13 October 2026.

Conclusion

The Connect & Create Relay Scheme 2026 offers young communications professionals in selected Sub-Saharan African countries an opportunity to combine practical cultural communications work with structured professional development.

Through an approximately 11-month programme, selected participants will work with Creative Tandem projects in their countries while receiving training in areas such as storytelling, social media, editorial strategy, and press relations. They will also receive individual mentoring, a training certificate, professional networking opportunities, and an allowance for communication activities associated with their supported project.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to journalists, communications professionals, content creators, influencers, and media presenters who already have two to five years of professional experience and have developed an active audience or meaningful local presence.

Applications are open from 15 September 2026 until 13 October 2026. Eligible professionals who are interested in cultural communications, performing arts, music, and the creative industries should review the official guidelines, prepare a strong CV and portfolio, and submit their application before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Do you have an innovative idea that could help businesses, communities, or cities become more sustainable, resource-efficient, and environmentally responsible?

The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is designed to help promising green and circular-economy ideas move from early concepts to practical, viable, and market-ready solutions.

The program supports university students, young innovators, researchers, startups, entrepreneurs, and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the West Bank, including Jerusalem, who are working on solutions related to the green and circular economy.

Through a combination of hackathons, specialized mentoring, technical assistance, incubation, networking, and seed funding, participants can receive practical support to develop, test, refine, and implement their ideas.

The program provides financial support averaging approximately €8,000 per selected team, together with technical assistance, mentoring, guidance, and incubation support for up to six months.

Applications for the InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program are scheduled to open in September 2026.

What Is InnoTadweer: EcoHack+?

InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ is an innovation and entrepreneurship support program focused on developing solutions that contribute to a greener and more circular economy in the West Bank.

The program is intended for people and organizations with ideas, prototypes, businesses, or existing facilities that could benefit from adopting more sustainable practices.

Rather than focusing only on generating ideas, EcoHack+ aims to help participants move through the development process toward practical implementation and market readiness.

The program combines several forms of support, including:

  • Hackathons
  • Technical assistance
  • Specialized mentoring
  • Expert guidance
  • Incubation
  • Networking
  • Multidisciplinary team formation
  • Seed funding
  • Support for testing and refining solutions
  • Assistance in moving ideas toward implementation and market readiness

This combination allows participants to address both the technical and business aspects of green innovation.

The Green and Circular Economy Focus

The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program focuses on innovations that can improve the way resources are produced, consumed, reused, recovered, and managed.

The green and circular economy approach seeks to reduce waste and resource consumption while creating sustainable economic opportunities.

The program welcomes ideas and solutions related to areas such as:

Resource Efficiency

Solutions that help businesses, organizations, communities, or other users make more efficient use of resources can be considered.

This may include innovations that reduce unnecessary consumption of materials, water, energy, or other resources.

Waste Valorization

EcoHack+ is interested in approaches that transform waste into economic value.

Instead of treating waste solely as something to dispose of, participants can explore ways to recover, reuse, process, or convert waste into useful materials, products, or other forms of value.

Circular Business Models

Participants can develop business models based on circular economy principles.

These may involve approaches that extend product lifecycles, encourage reuse, improve recycling, recover valuable materials, reduce waste, or create alternative approaches to resource consumption.

Renewable Energy

The program also welcomes innovative solutions related to renewable energy and the transition toward more sustainable energy systems.

Sustainable Production

Ideas that help businesses produce goods or services more sustainably can also fit within the program’s focus.

This can include approaches designed to reduce resource use, minimize waste, improve production efficiency, or incorporate environmentally responsible processes.

Green Technologies

EcoHack+ welcomes technological solutions that address environmental and sustainability challenges.

Green technologies can potentially be applied across different industries and sectors, depending on the specific challenge being addressed.

Sustainable Agriculture

The program also includes solutions related to sustainable agriculture and resource-efficient agricultural practices.

Participants can explore innovative approaches that contribute to more sustainable agricultural production and resource management.

Other Green and Circular Economy Challenges

The program is not limited to the examples listed above. It also welcomes other innovative approaches addressing challenges connected to the green and circular economy.

Who Can Participate?

InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ is designed for a broad range of innovators and organizations.

Potential participants include:

  • University students
  • Young innovators
  • Researchers
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Early-stage startups
  • Informal teams
  • Existing micro enterprises
  • Small enterprises
  • Medium enterprises

The program therefore accommodates participants at different stages of development, from individuals who have only an initial idea to businesses and organizations that already have an operating facility and want to introduce more sustainable practices.

Individual and Team Applications

Participants do not necessarily need to have an established team before applying.

Applications can be submitted:

  • Individually
  • As part of an existing team

For participants who apply individually, the program provides opportunities to connect with people from different disciplines, professional backgrounds, and areas of expertise.

This is particularly important because many environmental and circular-economy challenges require collaboration between people with different technical, business, scientific, entrepreneurial, and practical skills.

During the hackathon component, participants can receive support in developing multidisciplinary teams.

Track A: Idea Development

One of the program’s tracks is Track A – Idea Development.

This track is intended for participants who have an idea but may not yet know how to develop it into a practical solution.

It is particularly relevant to:

  • University students
  • Young innovators
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Informal teams
  • Individuals with early-stage ideas

The track focuses on early-stage idea development, particularly in the areas of:

  • Resource efficiency
  • Sustainable production
  • Green innovation
  • Circular economy solutions

Participants in this stage can use the program’s support to develop their initial concept and begin determining how it could become a viable solution.

From Idea to Market-Ready Solution

A major objective of EcoHack+ is to help participants progress through the different stages of innovation.

An idea may initially exist only as a concept. Through the program, participants can receive support to develop and refine that concept.

The development process can involve:

1. Identifying the Problem

Participants begin by understanding the environmental, resource-efficiency, or circular-economy problem they are attempting to solve.

A clearly defined problem can provide the foundation for developing a practical solution.

2. Developing the Idea

Participants can work on transforming an initial idea into a more clearly defined innovation or project.

This may involve identifying the target users, defining the proposed solution, and determining how the solution could address the identified challenge.

3. Building or Refining a Prototype

For participants who already have a prototype, the program can provide support to further develop and refine it.

The objective is to move beyond an initial concept toward something that can be tested and evaluated.

4. Mentoring and Technical Assistance

Participants receive access to technical assistance, specialized mentoring, and guidance.

Expert support can help participants identify challenges, improve their solutions, and consider technical and business requirements.

5. Incubation

Selected participants can receive incubation support for up to six months.

This provides additional time and support for developing the idea, project, or business.

6. Financial Support

Selected teams can receive financial support averaging approximately €8,000.

The funding can provide resources needed to advance a promising solution toward implementation and market readiness, subject to the program’s funding requirements and selection procedures.

Expected Benefits of the Program

Participants selected for InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ can benefit from several forms of support.

Financial Support

Selected teams are expected to receive financial support averaging around €8,000.

The funding component can help selected teams move their ideas forward and support the development of green or circular-economy solutions.

Technical Assistance

Participants can receive dedicated technical assistance relevant to developing and improving their solutions.

Specialized Mentoring

Expert mentors can provide guidance as participants develop their ideas, prototypes, projects, or businesses.

Incubation Support

Selected participants can receive incubation support for up to six months.

Networking Opportunities

Participants can connect with people from different professional and academic backgrounds.

This can help individuals find collaborators and build multidisciplinary teams.

Market Readiness

The program aims to help promising ideas progress toward implementation and market readiness.

This is particularly important for participants who want to transform an environmental concept into a practical product, service, business model, or project.

Who Might Benefit From Applying?

The program can be relevant to individuals and organizations at different stages.

For example, a university student with an early idea related to waste management could use the program to develop the concept further.

A young entrepreneur could use the program to refine a circular business model.

A researcher could explore how research findings can be translated into a practical green innovation.

An early-stage startup could receive mentoring and funding to improve an existing prototype.

An existing MSME could explore how to introduce more resource-efficient or sustainable practices into its operations.

The program’s broad structure allows different types of applicants to approach green innovation from different starting points.

Program Duration

The stated duration of the InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is:

18 months

Within this broader program period, participants can engage with different activities and forms of support depending on their track and stage of development.

Application Period

The application period is scheduled to open in:

September 2026

The information provided does not specify a final application deadline.

Applicants should therefore monitor the official InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ application information for the opening announcement, submission deadline, application requirements, and any updates to the program schedule.

Program Geographic Focus

The program is implemented in the West Bank, including Jerusalem.

Its focus is therefore on supporting green innovation, entrepreneurship, resource efficiency, and circular-economy development within the Palestinian context.

Applicants should review the official program eligibility requirements before applying to confirm their geographic eligibility.

Supporting Organizations

The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is implemented within the Green West Bank and SAWA 2 projects.

The program is supported by:

  • The European Union
  • The Belgian Government through DGD

Implementation is led by the Belgian Agency for International Cooperation (ENAPEL) in partnership with the Business Center for Innovation, Technology and Entrepreneurship (BCite) at Al-Quds University.

The collaboration brings together international development support and local innovation and entrepreneurship expertise.

Contribution to the Palestinian Green Economy

The program is part of broader efforts to support a greener and more circular Palestinian economy.

Through support for green innovation and entrepreneurship, the program seeks to contribute to:

  • Green innovation
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Business competitiveness
  • Resource efficiency
  • Sustainable production
  • Circular economy development
  • Environmental solutions
  • Market-oriented innovation

Supporting innovative businesses and young people can also contribute to the development of new products, services, business models, and technologies addressing environmental challenges.

Why Multidisciplinary Collaboration Matters

Many sustainability challenges cannot be solved through one area of expertise alone.

For example, developing a solution for waste valorization may require technical knowledge, environmental expertise, business planning, market research, finance, design, and communication.

Similarly, a renewable-energy innovation may require engineering expertise alongside entrepreneurship and business-development skills.

EcoHack+ therefore encourages participants from different backgrounds to collaborate.

Applicants who do not yet have a team can potentially use the hackathon and networking activities to meet other participants and form multidisciplinary teams.

What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying

Potential applicants should consider several questions before submitting an application.

Clearly Define the Problem

What environmental or resource-efficiency challenge does your idea address?

Explain the Proposed Solution

How does your idea address the problem?

Identify the Target Users

Who would use or benefit from the solution?

Consider Sustainability

How would the solution contribute to a greener or more circular economy?

Think About Feasibility

Can the idea realistically be developed, tested, implemented, or scaled?

Consider the Market

If the solution is commercial, who would pay for it and why?

Identify the Stage of Development

Is your idea:

  • An early concept?
  • A prototype?
  • An existing startup?
  • An established MSME looking to adopt sustainable practices?

Understanding the current stage of the project can help applicants determine which program track is most appropriate.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program provides a structured pathway for developing innovative solutions to environmental and resource-efficiency challenges in the West Bank, including Jerusalem.

By combining hackathons, technical assistance, specialized mentoring, networking, incubation, and seed funding, the program is designed to help participants move from an initial idea or existing project toward a more developed and potentially market-ready solution.

The program is open to different types of innovators, including university students, young innovators, researchers, early-stage startups, entrepreneurs, and micro, small and medium enterprises. Participants can apply individually or as teams, with opportunities to form multidisciplinary teams during the hackathon.

With average financial support of approximately €8,000 per selected team and incubation support of up to six months, EcoHack+ provides both financial and non-financial assistance to participants working on green and circular-economy solutions.

The application period is scheduled to open in September 2026. Since a specific closing date was not provided in the information available, interested applicants should monitor the official program announcement and application platform for the deadline and complete eligibility requirements.

Click HERE for more grant opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The Goldman Sachs 2026 Emerging Leaders Series is an exploratory career development program designed to introduce promising undergraduate and master’s students to future opportunities at one of the world’s leading financial services firms.

The program provides participants with an opportunity to explore different business areas at Goldman Sachs, develop professional and recruiting skills, interact with employees and senior leaders, and gain insight into the firm’s Summer Analyst opportunities.

Through business-specific training, interview preparation, networking activities, group exercises, and engagement with professionals, participants can gain a better understanding of the skills required to pursue future internship opportunities at Goldman Sachs.

Applications for the 2026 Emerging Leaders Series are currently open, with the application deadline set for Sunday, October 4, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET).

About the Goldman Sachs Emerging Leaders Series

The Emerging Leaders Series is an exploratory program intended to help students prepare for future recruiting opportunities at Goldman Sachs.

Rather than being a traditional internship, the program is designed to provide participants with early exposure to Goldman Sachs’ businesses and recruiting process.

Participants will have opportunities to:

  • Learn more about Goldman Sachs and its different business divisions.
  • Explore potential career paths within the firm.
  • Participate in business-specific training.
  • Develop professional and career-related skills.
  • Take part in interview preparation activities.
  • Participate in group activities.
  • Network with Goldman Sachs professionals.
  • Engage with senior leaders.
  • Learn more about future Summer Analyst opportunities.
  • Gain insights into the recruiting process.
  • Explore a specific Goldman Sachs business track.
  • Potentially visit one of Goldman Sachs’ offices in New York, Dallas, or Salt Lake City, depending on the business track.

The program is particularly relevant for students who are beginning to consider careers in financial services, investment banking, asset management, engineering, operations, risk, compliance, research, and other corporate functions.

What Is the Purpose of the Emerging Leaders Series?

The program is intended to help students develop the knowledge, professional skills, and understanding needed to navigate the early stages of a career at Goldman Sachs.

Students may use the experience to learn more about the firm’s business areas before applying for future internship opportunities.

The program combines several forms of professional development, including:

Business-Specific Training

Participants will receive exposure to a particular Goldman Sachs business track. This allows students to learn more about the work performed within different divisions and understand potential career paths within the organization.

Interview Preparation

The Emerging Leaders Series includes interview preparation designed to help participants better understand the recruiting process and prepare for future opportunities.

This can include developing an understanding of professional expectations, preparing for interviews, and becoming familiar with the skills and experiences that may be relevant to future Summer Analyst recruitment.

Networking

Networking is another central component of the program.

Participants will have opportunities to interact with Goldman Sachs professionals and potentially senior leaders. These interactions can help students learn about different career paths and gain first-hand perspectives on working within the firm.

Group Activities

Participants will also take part in group activities designed to encourage collaboration, communication, and engagement with other emerging professionals.

Goldman Sachs Emerging Leaders Series Business Tracks

As part of the program, participants will have the opportunity to immerse themselves in one of several business tracks.

The available tracks include:

1. FICC and Equities

FICC and Equities is part of Goldman Sachs’ markets-related business activities. Participants interested in sales and trading can use this track to learn more about careers involving financial markets, clients, products, and market activity.

2. Investment Banking

The Investment Banking track provides exposure to a major area of financial services involving corporate and institutional clients and financial transactions.

Students interested in investment banking can explore the type of work and professional skills associated with this career path.

3. Capital Solutions Group

The Capital Solutions Group track provides an opportunity to explore a business area focused on capital and financial solutions.

This may be relevant to students interested in financial strategy, capital markets, and corporate finance.

4. Asset Management

The Asset Management track is relevant to students interested in investment management and financial markets.

Participants can learn more about how professionals work with investments and financial portfolios.

5. Wealth Management

The Wealth Management track introduces students to careers involving financial planning, investment management, and relationships with individual and institutional clients.

6. Controllers

The Controllers track provides exposure to financial management, accounting, reporting, and related functions within a large global financial institution.

7. Engineering

Students interested in technology and software-related careers can explore the Engineering track.

This may be particularly relevant to students interested in technology, software engineering, data, systems, and financial technology.

8. Global Compliance

The Global Compliance track provides exposure to compliance functions within a global financial institution.

Participants can learn more about how financial organizations manage regulatory and compliance responsibilities.

9. Global Investment Research

The Global Investment Research track is relevant to students interested in research, financial markets, economics, companies, industries, and investment analysis.

10. Operations

The Operations track provides an opportunity to learn about the functions that support the firm’s businesses and financial activities.

11. Risk

The Risk track introduces participants to the role of risk management within a global financial institution.

Students interested in financial risk, analysis, controls, and decision-making may find this business area relevant to their career exploration.

Who Is the Goldman Sachs Emerging Leaders Series For?

The program is intended for undergraduate and master’s students who meet the specified graduation-year requirement.

According to the opportunity announcement, eligible students must be graduating between:

December 2028 and June 2029

This means applicants should carefully confirm that their expected graduation date falls within the stated period before submitting an application.

The program is designed to prepare participants for future Summer Analyst opportunities, making it particularly relevant to students who are still completing their undergraduate or master’s education and are beginning to prepare for internship recruitment.

Program Dates

The Goldman Sachs Emerging Leaders Series will take place between:

Fall 2026 and Spring 2027

The exact program schedule will vary depending on the selected business track.

Participants should therefore be prepared for the possibility that their specific program activities may occur at different times during the Fall 2026–Spring 2027 period.

Program Location

The program is listed as having a:

Virtual and potential in-person component

Depending on the selected business track, participants may have the opportunity to visit one of the following Goldman Sachs offices:

  • New York
  • Dallas
  • Salt Lake City

The opportunity information does not indicate that every participant will necessarily attend an in-person component. The specific arrangements may depend on the selected business track.

Event Time Zone

The listed event time zone is:

EST — U.S. Eastern Time

Applicants outside the United States should pay particular attention to the stated application deadline and convert the deadline to their local time to avoid missing it.

Dress Code

The listed dress code for the program is:

Business formal

Participants should therefore be prepared to meet a professional business dress standard for applicable program activities, particularly any in-person events.

Goldman Sachs Summer Analyst Opportunities
