item.content:encoded:
The Visa Foundation has launched the U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program, a new grant opportunity designed to strengthen nonprofit organizations that provide direct support to small and micro businesses across the United States.

Through the program, Visa Foundation is committing $2 million in grant funding to nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations (ESOs). Selected organizations will receive flexible, 12-month grants ranging from $100,000 to $250,000 to strengthen their capacity, expand their services, and help small and micro businesses become more resilient, competitive, and positioned for sustainable growth.

Applications are open and must be submitted by October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM (noon) Pacific Time.

The program is administered by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors (RPA), which is responsible for managing the Request for Proposals process and grantmaking activities.

Overview of the Visa Foundation Grant Program

Small and micro businesses play an important role in creating employment, generating income, supporting local communities, and contributing to economic development. However, many small businesses face challenges in accessing the knowledge, technical assistance, technology, training, and other resources required to grow and remain competitive.

The Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program seeks to address some of these challenges indirectly by investing in organizations that already work closely with small and micro businesses.

Rather than providing grants directly to individual entrepreneurs, the program provides funding to nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations that deliver services to operating small and micro businesses.

The goal is therefore to strengthen the organizations that make up the small-business support ecosystem and enable them to reach more businesses, improve their services, and increase their impact.

According to the program information, Visa Foundation is committing $2 million to the initiative, while RPA is administering the application and grantmaking process.

What Funding Is Available?

Successful applicants are expected to receive grants ranging from:

  • $100,000 to $250,000
  • 12-month grant period
  • Grants beginning in January 2027
  • Flexible funding that can support both programming and organizational operations

The exact grant amount will be determined in relation to the size of the applicant organization.

This flexibility is an important feature of the opportunity because organizations can use the funding to strengthen both the services they provide and the internal capacity required to deliver those services effectively.

What Can the Grant Funding Be Used For?

The program allows grant funding to support a broad range of activities connected to strengthening an organization’s ability to serve small and micro businesses.

Eligible uses may include:

1. Business Training

Organizations can use funding to strengthen or expand training programs that provide entrepreneurs and business owners with practical knowledge and skills.

Training may form part of an organization’s existing programming or be introduced or expanded through the grant.

2. Technical Assistance

Funding can support technical assistance designed to help small and micro businesses overcome specific operational or business-development challenges.

3. Business Coaching

Organizations may use grant resources to expand coaching and support services that help operating businesses make informed decisions and improve their resilience and growth prospects.

4. Digital Adoption and Technology

The program recognizes the growing importance of technology and digital tools for small businesses.

Funding may therefore support services that help businesses adopt technology, use digital tools, and respond to changing market conditions.

The program specifically identifies helping small and micro businesses navigate AI, digital tools, and technology adoption as an area that may receive priority consideration.

5. Staffing

Grant resources can also contribute to organizational staffing needs where this strengthens the applicant’s capacity to provide direct services to small and micro businesses.

6. Administrative and Operational Costs

The funding is flexible enough to support certain operational needs, including administrative costs, where those expenses contribute to the organization’s ability to deliver and expand its work.

Applicants will need to explain how the requested funding would strengthen their organization and increase its impact on the small-business community.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The opportunity is intended for nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations (ESOs) that directly support operating small and micro businesses.

To qualify, an organization must meet the program’s eligibility requirements.

U.S. 501(c)(3) Status

Applicants must be U.S.-based public charities with valid 501(c)(3) status and must comply with applicable 501(c)(3) requirements.

Organizational Budget

Applicants must have an annual operating budget between:

$1 million and $10 million.

This requirement means the program is aimed at established, mid-sized to large organizations rather than very early-stage nonprofit organizations.

Direct Services to Small and Micro Businesses

Organizations must directly provide business-support services to operating small and micro businesses.

Examples of qualifying services include:

  • Business training
  • Coaching
  • Technical assistance
  • Peer learning
  • Technology adoption support

The purpose of these services should be to help small and micro businesses strengthen their growth, resilience, and competitiveness.

Financial Documentation

Applicants must have two years of audited financial statements and/or IRS Form 990s.

Applicants will also need to provide their current board-approved operating budget showing anticipated revenues and expenses for 2026 and 2027.

Can Fiscally Sponsored Organizations Apply?

Yes.

Fiscally sponsored organizations can apply if their fiscal sponsor has valid 501(c)(3) status and the fiscally sponsored organization meets all other eligibility requirements.

Additional documentation may be required, including:

  • Fiscal sponsor governance materials
  • List of directors and their affiliations
  • Two years of audited financials
  • IRS Form 990
  • Signed fiscal sponsorship agreement or memorandum of understanding

Therefore, being fiscally sponsored does not automatically exclude an organization from consideration.

Can Local Chapters of National Organizations Apply?

Yes, local chapters may be considered if they have standalone 501(c)(3) status and meet the remaining eligibility requirements.

Organizations should therefore carefully verify their legal and financial structure before beginning an application.

Can Previous Visa Foundation Grantees Apply?

Yes.

Past and current grantees of Visa Foundation or Visa Inc. are eligible to apply, provided they meet the other requirements of the program.

What Types of Small Businesses Does the Program Support?

The program defines small and micro businesses as independently owned businesses that are currently operating and actively selling products or services.

While there are no strict numerical cutoffs, the program states that qualifying businesses would generally have:

  • 50 or fewer employees
  • $1.5 million or less in annual revenue

The focus is therefore on operating businesses rather than individuals who are only considering starting a business.

What Organizations May Be Particularly Competitive?

Although all eligible applications will be reviewed, the program identifies several characteristics that may strengthen an organization’s application.

Organizations are encouraged to demonstrate:

  1. A strong understanding of small and micro business challenges and opportunities
  2. Trusted relationships with the communities they serve
  3. The ability to adapt to changing market needs
  4. Experience helping businesses use AI, digital tools, and technology
  5. Meaningful and measurable impact on business growth and resilience
  6. A commitment to continuous learning and collaboration
  7. The organizational capacity to strengthen or expand services using grant funding

These priorities indicate that applicants should be able to demonstrate not only what they do, but also the measurable difference their services make for the businesses they support.

Which Organizations May Be Less Competitive?

The program states that eligible organizations may be less competitive if they:

  • Are not primarily focused on providing direct business-support services to small and micro businesses.
  • Primarily support aspiring entrepreneurs or idea-stage businesses rather than currently operating businesses.
  • Reach fewer than 200 small and micro businesses per year.
  • Cannot demonstrate outcomes or evidence of impact.
  • Propose grant uses that are not clearly connected to strengthening small-business growth and resilience.

Meeting the basic eligibility requirements therefore does not necessarily mean that an organization will receive funding. Applicants should clearly demonstrate their track record, reach, measurable outcomes, and connection between the proposed funding and improved services for operating small and micro businesses.

Is the Program Focused on Particular Industries?

No.

The program does not prioritize a specific industry or business sector.

Instead, it is designed to strengthen Entrepreneurial Support Organizations that provide effective business-support services to small and micro businesses across the United States.

When selecting organizations, the program will consider how the overall group of grantees represents different:

  • Geographic areas
  • Service models
  • Communities served

This approach means that applicants do not need to operate in one particular industry to be considered.

How Does the Application Process Work?

Applications must be submitted through the designated online application portal.

Applicants will need to create an account and register their organization because the program is accepting applications from verified organizations.

The application portal is administered through SurveyMonkey Apply.

Importantly, applications cannot be submitted by email.

Applicants can also review the application questions in advance through the program’s application-question document.

Required Financial Documents

Applicants should prepare their financial documentation before submitting an application.

The program requires:

  • Audited financial statements for the organization’s two most recently completed fiscal years; or
  • Two years of IRS Form 990s if audited financial statements are not available.
  • The organization’s current board-approved operating budget showing anticipated revenues and expenses for 2026 and 2027.

Having these documents ready can help organizations prepare their applications efficiently and ensure that required financial information is available before the deadline.

How Many Applications Can an Organization Submit?

Organizations may submit only one application per EIN/organization.

Applicants should therefore make sure that their submission represents the organization’s strongest and most complete application before final submission.

When Will Applicants Receive a Decision?

Applicants can expect to be notified of funding decisions by January 2027.

Successful grants will be one-time awards lasting 12 months, beginning in January 2027.

What Happens After Organizations Receive Funding?

Selected grantees will participate in the grant program for 12 months.

Visa Foundation also plans to facilitate engagement opportunities throughout the grant period. These activities are intended to allow grantees to share:

  • Lessons learned
  • Challenges
  • Best practices
  • Experiences from implementing their programs

This creates an opportunity for participating organizations to learn from one another while implementing their funded activities.

Reporting Requirements

Organizations receiving funding will be expected to submit a final narrative and financial report to Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors.

The final reporting process will cover areas including:

  • Progress made during the grant period
  • Results achieved
  • Lessons learned
  • Key performance indicators

Examples of indicators specifically identified by the program include:

  • Number of small and micro businesses reached
  • Number of jobs supported
  • Revenue growth among supported businesses

Applicants should therefore consider how they currently measure impact and how they will demonstrate results during the grant period.

Important Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting an application is:

October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM (noon) Pacific Time.

Late applications will not be considered.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications, particularly because the application requires organizational registration and supporting financial documentation.

APPLY HERE

Important Confidentiality and Application Terms

Applicants should also pay attention to the terms governing application submissions.

The program states that application submissions will not be treated as confidential. Applicants should therefore avoid including proprietary information, trade secrets, or other confidential information that they want to keep protected.

Application information may be shared with Visa Foundation’s program partners, including Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors and Maigent Partners, for program evaluation, administration, and reporting.

The application information will be handled according to the Visa Privacy Policy and related application terms.

By submitting an application, organizations also grant Visa Foundation a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and distribute application materials for purposes related to program evaluation, administration, and reporting. The terms specify that this license does not transfer ownership of intellectual property to Visa Foundation.

Who Makes the Final Grant Decisions?

Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors is administering the program and the Request for Proposals process.

As the legal grantor of record, RPA ultimately holds final authority over grantmaking decisions.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFORMATION ON Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program

Questions About the Program

Applicants with programmatic questions can contact:

EntrepreneurialSupportRFP@rockpa.org

For grant-management questions, applicants can contact:

grantsmanagement@rockpa.org

Applicants are encouraged to review the available FAQs before contacting the program team. The organizers note that, because of the expected volume of inquiries, they may not be able to respond to every question before the application deadline. They also do not provide feedback on individual applications or proposals.

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Program Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program
Opportunity Type Grant
Total Funding Commitment $2 million
Individual Grant Size $100,000–$250,000
Grant Duration 12 months
Expected Start January 2027
Target Applicants Nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations
Geographic Focus United States
Eligible Areas 50 U.S. states, Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories
Required Legal Status U.S.-based 501(c)(3) public charity
Annual Budget Requirement $1 million–$10 million
Financial History Two years of audited financial statements and/or IRS Form 990s
Primary Beneficiaries Operating small and micro businesses
Typical SMB Profile Generally 50 or fewer employees and $1.5 million or less in annual revenue
Application Deadline October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM PT
Decision Timeline By January 2027
Applications by Email Not accepted

Conclusion

The Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program provides a significant funding opportunity for established nonprofit organizations working directly with small and micro businesses in the United States.

With grants ranging from $100,000 to $250,000, the program is intended to strengthen organizational capacity rather than simply finance individual business ideas. Eligible organizations can use the flexible funding to expand training, coaching, technical assistance, digital adoption initiatives, staffing, administrative capacity, and other activities that strengthen their ability to serve operating small and micro businesses.

Organizations considering applying should carefully assess their eligibility, particularly their 501(c)(3) status, U.S. geographic focus, $1 million–$10 million annual operating budget, direct-service track record, financial documentation, and demonstrated impact on small and micro businesses.

Applicants should also ensure that their proposed use of funds is clearly connected to improving business growth and resilience and that they can demonstrate measurable outcomes.

The application deadline is October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM Pacific Time, and late applications will not be accepted. Organizations interested in applying should begin preparing their financial documents, organizational information, impact evidence, and proposed use of funds well before the deadline.

Empowering the Next Chapter: Girls Leadership Seeks a Visionary Chief Executive Officer
​Carrington Talent Group is managing a nationwide executive search for the next Chief Executive Officer of Girls Leadership, a national nonprofit dedicated to the social and emotional development of girls and gender-expansive youth. Operating at a pivotal inflection point, this fully remote, US-based leadership role offers an exceptional opportunity to steer a $2 million organization toward expanded national impact, programmatic depth, and long-term financial sustainability.
​About Girls Leadership
​Girls grow up hearing that their voices are too loud and their power should be managed rather than celebrated. Girls Leadership challenges this paradigm by equipping the adults who shape girls’ daily lives—teachers, coaches, counselors, and family service providers—with the tools to build environments where girls learn to use their voices, trust their power, and lead authentically.
​The organization’s unique model relies on three core pillars:
​Working through influential adult multipliers across classrooms, teams, and communities.
​Centering social-emotional learning (SEL) as the foundation of all curricula.
​Co-designing programs first with marginalized girls to ensure solutions serve every girl effectively.
​Key Responsibilities
​Strategic Leadership: Partner with the Board to establish multi-year strategies, translate vision into execution, and maintain executive oversight of organizational financial health and operational systems.
​Fundraising & Revenue Expansion: Collaborate with the Chief Development Officer and Board to secure six- and seven-figure gifts, diversify revenue streams, and expand corporate, philanthropic, and earned-income partnerships.
​People Management: Inspire, coach, and support a remote team of 10 full-time equivalent employees, fostering a culture of inclusion, belonging, and data-informed learning.
​Governance: Partner with the Board of Directors to ensure strong governance, strategic oversight, transparency, and board recruitment.
​Required Experience & Skills
​Minimum of 7 years of enterprise-level executive leadership experience in the nonprofit or social impact sector.
​Proven track record of successful fundraising and revenue generation (securing 6- and 7-figure gifts).
​Deep commitment to gender and racial equity, with lived experience or professional alignment to the communities served.
​Strong understanding of cash-flow management, budgeting, and financial forecasting.
​Willingness and ability to undertake regular domestic travel.
​Compensation & Benefits
​Base Salary: $170,000 to $200,000, commensurate with experience.
​Health Coverage: Comprehensive health insurance with 99% of employee premiums covered by the employer, plus optional dental and vision.
​Paid Time Off: 2 weeks of PTO, 1 week of paid sick leave, 11 paid holidays, and 4 weeks of paid office closures annually (two weeks in July and two weeks in December).
​Additional Perks: 401(k) retirement plan after one year of service and monthly phone/internet stipends.
​Priority application deadline: October 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM ET.
​Opportunity Category
​Job
​Eligibility and Qualifications Overview
​Target Audience: Senior executives, nonprofit directors, and social impact leaders.
​Eligible Region / Location: United States (Remote position requiring regular domestic travel; applicants must be authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship).
​Diversity & Background: Open to a diverse pool of candidates from all racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds sharing a commitment to gender and racial equity

item.content:encoded:
Are you a mid-level professional looking to strengthen your leadership capabilities, develop greater self-awareness, build resilience, and learn how to mobilise people to create meaningful change? The UONGOZI Institute Emerging Leaders Programme 2026–2027 offers an intensive six-month leadership development experience designed for mid-level executives working across different sectors in Africa.

The programme is delivered by UONGOZI Institute in collaboration with the HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management and combines predominantly online learning with selected face-to-face sessions. It brings together leadership development expertise from around the world and is designed to help participants examine their leadership approaches, strengthen their ability to respond to challenges, and develop the capacity to lead change effectively.

The Emerging Leaders Programme 2026–2027 begins in December 2026 and runs for six months. Applications must be received by Friday, 23 October 2026 at 23:00 hours (EAT).

A limited number of merit-based scholarships are also available for eligible applicants.

About the UONGOZI Institute Emerging Leaders Programme

The Emerging Leaders Programme is a leadership development programme created for mid-level executives working in any sector across Africa.

Rather than focusing exclusively on technical professional skills, the programme is designed around broader leadership capabilities. Participants are challenged to reflect on their own leadership practices, understand their strengths and areas for development, cultivate resilience and a growth mindset, and learn how to mobilise others toward meaningful change.

The programme is delivered over a period of six months and consists of six modules.

Participants will learn through a blended model consisting of:

  • 85% e-learning
  • 15% face-to-face sessions

This delivery structure allows working professionals to participate in a largely flexible learning environment while still benefiting from opportunities for direct interaction and engagement.

The programme’s faculty consists of leadership development experts from across the world, providing participants with exposure to perspectives and approaches from different professional and geographic contexts.

Emerging Leaders Programme 2026–2027 at a Glance

Programme Detail Information
Programme Emerging Leaders Programme
Organiser UONGOZI Institute
Partner HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management
Target participants Mid-level executives across Africa
Programme start December 2026
Duration 6 months
Number of modules 6
Delivery 85% e-learning and 15% face-to-face
Tuition fee TZS 2.6 million per person
Payment option Two instalments
Scholarships Limited merit-based scholarships available
Application deadline 23 October 2026
Deadline time 23:00 hours EAT

Who Is the Emerging Leaders Programme For?

The programme is specifically designed for mid-level executives working in any sector across Africa.

This means that applicants do not have to come from one particular professional field. Professionals working in different sectors may apply as long as they satisfy the programme’s requirements.

The programme may therefore be relevant to professionals working in areas such as:

  • Government and public administration
  • Business and private-sector organisations
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • International development
  • Education
  • Finance
  • Technology
  • Health
  • Civil society
  • Social enterprises
  • Research and academia
  • Other professional sectors

The central focus is not the applicant’s specific sector but their professional experience, leadership responsibilities, and potential for further leadership development.

Key Objectives of the Emerging Leaders Programme

The programme is structured around several important dimensions of leadership development.

1. Building Self-Awareness

Effective leadership begins with understanding oneself.

The programme challenges participants to examine their leadership approaches and develop greater awareness of their own:

  • Strengths
  • Challenges
  • Leadership behaviours
  • Decision-making approaches
  • Professional experiences
  • Areas requiring further development

Developing self-awareness can help leaders better understand how their actions affect colleagues, teams, organisations, and other stakeholders.

2. Developing Resilience

Leadership often involves navigating uncertainty, pressure, organisational change, and difficult decisions.

The Emerging Leaders Programme seeks to help participants embrace a mindset of resilience, enabling them to approach challenges as part of the leadership process.

Rather than focusing only on immediate professional responsibilities, the programme encourages participants to develop the mindset and capabilities needed to continue learning and adapting when circumstances change.

3. Embracing a Growth Mindset

The programme also encourages participants to adopt a growth-oriented approach to leadership.

This involves recognising that leadership capabilities can be developed through:

  • Reflection
  • Learning
  • Experience
  • Feedback
  • Adaptation
  • Continuous improvement

For mid-level executives preparing to take on greater responsibilities, this approach can support continued professional and leadership development.

4. Mobilising Others to Drive Change

Leadership is not only about individual performance.

The Emerging Leaders Programme also focuses on the ability to mobilise others to drive change.

This is particularly relevant for professionals who work with teams, organisations, communities, stakeholders, or institutions and need to bring people together around shared objectives.

Participants are expected to explore leadership in ways that go beyond managing their own responsibilities and consider how they can influence and engage others to contribute to change.

Six-Month Programme Structure

The Emerging Leaders Programme consists of six modules delivered over six months.

The source indicates that the programme starts in December 2026 and runs for six months.

The combination of multiple modules allows participants to engage with leadership development progressively rather than through a single short training event.

The programme’s self-paced approach also provides flexibility for mid-level executives who may have ongoing professional responsibilities.

Programme Delivery: 85% Online and 15% Face-to-Face

One of the defining features of the Emerging Leaders Programme is its blended delivery model.

The programme consists of:

85% E-Learning

The majority of the programme is delivered through e-learning.

This approach provides participants with greater flexibility to engage with the programme alongside their professional responsibilities.

15% Face-to-Face Sessions

The remaining portion of the programme involves face-to-face sessions.

These sessions provide opportunities for direct engagement and interaction that complement the online learning component.

The combination of online and face-to-face learning creates a blended learning experience rather than a programme that relies exclusively on either digital or physical instruction.

International Faculty and Leadership Expertise

The programme brings together a faculty consisting of experts in leadership development from across the world.

This international faculty is intended to expose participants to leadership perspectives and expertise beyond their immediate professional environments.

For African executives, such exposure can provide an opportunity to examine leadership challenges from multiple perspectives and consider how different approaches may apply to their own organisational and professional contexts.

Collaboration With HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management

The Emerging Leaders Programme is undertaken by UONGOZI Institute in collaboration with HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management.

HAUS is a Finnish public management organisation, and its involvement contributes to the programme’s international leadership-development dimension.

The collaboration brings together expertise from different institutional and geographic contexts in the delivery of the programme.

Programme Duration

The Emerging Leaders Programme has a total duration of:

Six months

The programme is scheduled to start in December 2026.

This extended format gives participants time to engage with the programme’s six modules rather than completing all learning activities within a short workshop or seminar.

Tuition Fee

The tuition fee for the programme is:

TZS 2.6 million per person

Applicants should take this cost into consideration when preparing their application and planning their participation.

However, the institute provides an instalment payment option.

Tuition Fee Payment in Two Instalments

Participants have the option to pay the tuition fee in two instalments.

The payment structure is:

First Instalment

50% of the tuition fee

This is payable in advance of registration in November.

Second Instalment

50% of the tuition fee

This is payable in advance of Module 4 in February.

This instalment structure gives successful participants an alternative to paying the entire programme fee at once.

Merit-Based Scholarships

A limited number of merit-based scholarships are available for the Emerging Leaders Programme.

This means that applicants who may not be able to cover the full tuition fee should still consider applying and reviewing the scholarship provisions.

Because the source describes the scholarships as limited and merit-based, applicants should not assume that every successful programme applicant will automatically receive financial support.

Applicants should therefore prepare their applications carefully and ensure that they meet the stated programme and selection requirements.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must have at least one year of supervisory, managerial, or leadership experience.

This requirement reflects the programme’s focus on mid-level executives rather than individuals who are completely new to professional leadership.

2. Professional Experience

Applicants must have a minimum of:

Five years of work experience

This requirement ensures that participants enter the programme with meaningful professional experience on which they can reflect and build.

3. Academic Qualification

Applicants must hold:

A bachelor’s degree or equivalent

The programme therefore expects applicants to have completed an undergraduate-level qualification or an equivalent credential.

4. English Language Skills

Applicants must have a:

Good command of written and spoken English

Because the programme includes e-learning and interaction with faculty and other participants, applicants need sufficient English proficiency to engage effectively with the programme.

5. Computer Skills

Applicants must have:

Excellent computer skills

This requirement is particularly relevant because 85% of the programme is delivered through e-learning.

Participants should therefore be comfortable using digital tools and engaging with online learning environments.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit several documents and pieces of information.

The application consists of three principal supporting requirements:

  1. Curriculum vitae
  2. Recommendation, commitment and permission letter from the employer
  3. Motivational statement

Each requirement serves a different purpose in demonstrating the applicant’s professional experience, organisational support, leadership background, and motivation for participating.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a curriculum vitae that:

  • Does not exceed three pages
  • Clearly presents their professional experience
  • Demonstrates relevant leadership or management experience
  • Provides information that allows the selection team to assess their professional background

Applicants should ensure that their CV stays within the three-page limit.

The application system accepts CV files in:

  • PDF
  • DOC
  • DOCX

2. Employer Recommendation, Commitment and Permission Letter

Applicants must provide a:

Recommendation, commitment and permission letter from their employer

This requirement demonstrates that the applicant’s organisation is aware of and supportive of their participation in the programme.

Applicants should therefore arrange this letter well before the application deadline.

The application system accepts the employer letter in:

  • PDF
  • DOC
  • DOCX
  • JPG
  • JPEG
  • PNG

3. Motivational Statement

Applicants must provide a motivational statement of:

450–500 words

The statement should explain three central areas:

  • Your leadership successes
  • Your leadership challenges
  • Your reasons for applying for the programme

This is an important part of the application because it gives candidates an opportunity to explain their leadership journey and why they believe the Emerging Leaders Programme is relevant to their professional development.

Applicants should remain within the specified 450–500 word range.

What Information Is Required in the Application Form?

The application form requests information in several sections.

Personal Details

Applicants are asked to provide:

  • First name
  • Middle name
  • Last name
  • Gender
  • Age group
  • Title, such as Ms, Mrs, Mr, Dr, Prof, or Eng
  • Email address
  • Phone number
  • Nationality
  • LinkedIn profile

Job Details

Applicants must also provide information about their current employment, including:

  • Organisation
  • Position
  • Postal address
  • Street
  • Region
  • Country

The form also asks applicants to identify the sector in which their organisation operates.

How Did You Hear About the Programme?

Applicants are asked how they learned about the Emerging Leaders Programme.

The available options include:

  • UONGOZI Institute’s website
  • Facebook
  • X (Twitter)
  • Instagram
  • LinkedIn
  • YouTube
  • WhatsApp
  • Colleague or friend
  • Internet search, such as Google or Safari
  • Other

Applicants can select the option that accurately reflects how they discovered the opportunity.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Emerging Leaders Programme 2026–2027 is:

Friday, 23 October 2026 at 23:00 hours EAT

Applications received after this deadline will not be considered.

Applicants should therefore submit their complete applications before the stated deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

The institute also states that only successful candidates will be contacted.

Important Programme Dates

Application deadline

Applications must be received by 23:00 EAT.

November 2026

First tuition instalment

December 2026

Programme begins

The six-month Emerging Leaders Programme starts.

February

Second tuition instalment

Why Consider the Emerging Leaders Programme?

The programme is designed around the development of leadership capabilities that can be relevant across sectors and professional environments.

Participants can expect the programme to provide an opportunity to:

  • Reflect on their leadership strengths and challenges
  • Develop greater self-awareness
  • Strengthen resilience
  • Embrace a growth mindset
  • Develop their ability to mobilise others
  • Learn from international leadership-development experts
  • Participate in a six-month structured development programme
  • Combine flexible online learning with face-to-face engagement
  • Connect with other professionals from across Africa
  • Apply leadership learning within their professional environments

The programme’s cross-sector approach also means that participants can come from different professional backgrounds rather than one specialised industry.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The programme may be particularly relevant to professionals who:

  • Have already taken on supervisory or managerial responsibilities
  • Have at least five years of professional experience
  • Want to strengthen their leadership capabilities
  • Are preparing for increased leadership responsibilities
  • Want to improve their ability to lead teams and mobilise others
  • Are interested in resilience and personal development
  • Want to develop a broader understanding of leadership
  • Can commit to a six-month learning programme
  • Are comfortable with online learning
  • Work in any sector across Africa

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should begin preparing their materials well before the deadline.

Step 1: Review Your Leadership Experience

Identify examples that demonstrate your experience in:

  • Supervising others
  • Managing teams
  • Leading projects
  • Solving organisational challenges
  • Driving change
  • Supporting colleagues
  • Taking responsibility for outcomes

These examples can help you demonstrate that you meet the leadership experience requirement.

Step 2: Prepare a Focused Three-Page CV

Make sure your CV does not exceed three pages.

Prioritise information relevant to your professional development and leadership experience.

Step 3: Request the Employer Letter Early

The employer recommendation, commitment and permission letter is a required part of the application.

Request it early enough to avoid delays close to the deadline.

Step 4: Develop Your Motivational Statement

Your statement must be 450–500 words and should address:

  1. Your leadership successes

  3. Why you want to participate in the programme

A clear and focused statement can help the selection team understand your motivation and professional development goals.

Step 5: Check Your Digital Documents

item.content:encoded:
Are you a university student seeking to build a career in international journalism, gain practical reporting experience, and develop your professional network with journalists around the world? The Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards 2027 provide financial support and professional opportunities for students interested in pursuing international journalism.

The program typically awards 18 Scholar Awards each year. Depending on the award, recipients receive either a $3,000 scholarship for independent academic or journalistic work or a $4,000 fellowship that can support time working in the bureau of a leading news organization, including organizations such as the Associated Press, Reuters, and Bloomberg.

The program is particularly focused on helping students launch careers in international journalism rather than supporting established mid-career professionals. Applicants can be of any nationality, provided they meet the program’s stated eligibility requirements.

The application deadline is Sunday, November 15, 2026.

About the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards

The Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards are designed to support emerging journalists who want to develop careers focused on international journalism.

The program provides students with both financial assistance and opportunities to strengthen their journalism careers. In a typical year, the Foundation grants 18 awards, with recipients receiving either:

  • A $3,000 scholarship to support independent work; or
  • A $4,000 fellowship that can be used to fund time in the bureau of a leading news organization.

Examples of organizations associated with fellowship placements include the Associated Press, Reuters, and Bloomberg.

The program is primarily aimed at students who want to pursue international journalism as a career, making it particularly relevant for aspiring reporters, photojournalists, video journalists, and audio journalists interested in international issues and communities.

Who Is the Overseas Press Club Foundation Looking For?

The program is intended for students who are building their journalism careers and have demonstrated an interest in international journalism.

The Foundation specifically states that applicants should be:

  • College juniors;
  • College seniors; or
  • Graduate students;
  • Enrolled in a degree program at the application deadline; and
  • Demonstrably interested in international journalism.

Applicants must also be currently enrolled full-time in a university program and satisfy one of the specified eligibility pathways:

  1. Be an international student studying at a U.S. college or university; or
  2. Be a U.S. citizen studying abroad.

The Foundation notes that its program is aimed at students of whatever nationality who want to pursue international journalism rather than simply return to their countries of origin to work as local reporters.

What Funding Is Available?

The Scholar Awards generally provide two forms of financial support.

$3,000 Scholarship

Some award recipients receive a $3,000 scholarship intended to support independent work and academic or journalistic goals.

This can be particularly relevant for students who are developing independent journalism projects or pursuing academic goals connected to international journalism.

$4,000 Fellowship

Other recipients receive a $4,000 fellowship that can be used to fund time in a bureau of a leading news organization.

The Foundation gives the Associated Press, Reuters, and Bloomberg as examples of major news organizations where such fellowship experiences may take place.

The distinction means applicants should consider how their proposed work and career goals align with the type of support they hope to receive.

What Does the Application Require?

The application consists of three major components:

  1. A cover letter
  2. A resume
  3. A journalism work sample

Applicants should prepare each component carefully because the Foundation provides specific instructions for each part of the submission.

1. Cover Letter

The cover letter should be one page and autobiographical in nature.

Applicants should use the letter to explain their development as a journalist and their reasons for pursuing international journalism.

The Foundation suggests addressing questions such as:

  • How did you develop an interest in journalism?
  • Why are you interested in a particular part of the world?
  • What international communities or issues interest you?
  • How would you use the scholarship or fellowship to advance your journalism career?
  • Are there any gaps or unusual leaps in your academic or professional progress that should be explained?

The cover letter therefore provides an opportunity to connect the applicant’s personal development, journalistic interests, international focus, and future career plans.

2. Resume

Applicants must submit a one-page resume.

The Foundation recommends emphasizing journalism-related experience and skills rather than providing an unnecessarily broad account of every activity.

The resume should highlight:

  • Previous journalism experience
  • Language skills
  • Media skills
  • Visa or passport status relevant to working overseas
  • International postings
  • Domestic postings
  • Published freelance work
  • Independent unpublished journalism projects

This information can help demonstrate both the applicant’s journalism background and their ability to work in international settings.

3. Journalism Work Sample

Applicants must select one type of work sample from the following categories:

  • Print journalism
  • Photojournalism
  • Video journalism
  • Audio journalism

The requirements differ depending on the format selected.

Print Journalism Work Sample

Applicants choosing print journalism must submit a 600–800 word writing sample.

The sample should focus on:

  • An area of the world; or
  • An international issue

The topic should be consistent with the applicant’s interests and experience.

Applicants should also explain whether the work:

  • Was previously published;
  • Was edited or condensed;
  • Was created as a school project.

The Foundation provides examples of previous winning topics that have covered diverse international subjects, demonstrating that applicants do not necessarily need to report on conventional foreign-policy topics.

Importantly, applicants do not need to have traveled abroad to apply. The Foundation notes that previous scholars have produced successful work about international communities and issues located within the United States, including reporting on Syrian and Lebanese immigrants in Brooklyn and Ukrainian refugees on Long Island.

Important submission rule for writing samples

Applicants should not send clips or URLs as their writing sample.

Instead, the work should be reformatted into a standalone document. Applicants may include links to their other work on their resume.

Photojournalism Work Sample

Applicants choosing photojournalism should submit either:

  • One PDF containing their photographs; or
  • A link to a website where judges can view the work online.

The entry can take the form of:

  • A feature;
  • A personality piece; or
  • A news journalism project.

The work may be narrated or may rely entirely on interviews and verité.

Applicants must also provide a writing sample of approximately 500 words explaining the photographs.

The written component should contextualize the images and explain:

  • How the photographs were captured; and/or
  • Why the photographs are significant.

This means the application evaluates not only the images themselves but also the applicant’s ability to explain the journalistic purpose and context of the work.

Video and Audio Journalism Work Sample

Applicants submitting video or audio work should provide a link where judges can view or listen to the submission.

The work can be:

  • A feature;
  • A personality piece; or
  • A news journalism piece.

It can be narrated or rely primarily on interviews and verité.

Length requirement

The video or audio entry must be:

  • At least 2 minutes long; and
  • No longer than 7 minutes.

The content should primarily have international interest.

Applicants must also provide an approximately 500-word written explanation contextualizing the work.

The explanation should address:

  • How the images or audio were captured;
  • Why the work is significant;
  • What role the applicant played in producing it; and
  • Appropriate credit for all team members who contributed.

Each video or audio submission should demonstrate the full arc of the story, with a beginning, middle, and end.

How to Submit the Application

The Foundation requires applicants to combine all application elements into a single document.

The accepted file formats are:

  • .docx
  • .pdf

The document should be named using the following format:

Last name_First name

The file must not exceed 10 MB.

Applicants can submit their application through the official submission page:

Submit the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Award Application

Application Deadline

The deadline for the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards is:

Sunday, November 15, 2026

Applicants should complete and submit all required materials before the deadline.

What Makes a Strong Application?

The Foundation provides several pieces of guidance about what judges respond well to.

According to the application information, judges respond positively to applications demonstrating:

  • Strong original reporting skills
  • Color
  • A clear sense of perspective
  • A clear beginning, middle, and end

Applicants are also advised to carefully proofread their materials. Applications that are exceedingly long may be disqualified, so candidates should follow the specified length requirements rather than adding unnecessary material.

This makes it important for applicants to focus on the quality and clarity of their journalism rather than simply submitting a large quantity of work.

International Business and Economic Journalism

The Foundation has a specific area of interest in international business and economic coverage.

Of the 18 awards, four are reserved for international business or economic coverage. The Foundation therefore encourages applicants interested in these areas to submit work demonstrating a strong understanding of global economic topics.

Relevant topics mentioned by the Foundation include:

  • Trade
  • Finance
  • Emerging markets
  • Immigration
  • Climate
  • Public health

Applicants interested in these areas can therefore consider submitting work that demonstrates their ability to report on global economic and interconnected international issues.

AI Use and Originality Requirements

The Foundation places an explicit requirement on the originality of application materials.

All application material must be the result of the applicant’s own journalism work.

The Foundation also states that any use of AI must be:

  • Responsible; and
  • Clearly disclosed.

Applicants should therefore make sure that their submitted journalism accurately represents their own reporting and that any AI use is disclosed according to the Foundation’s requirement.

Language Requirement

All application materials must be submitted in English.

If an applicant’s original work was produced in another language, an English translation must be provided.

This requirement applies to the application materials and should be taken into consideration when preparing a work sample originally produced in another language.

Applicants Do Not Need International Travel Experience

One potentially important point for aspiring international journalists is that applicants do not have to have traveled abroad to apply.

The Foundation’s examples demonstrate that international journalism can involve reporting on international communities and global issues within the United States.

Previous scholars have reported on:

  • Syrian and Lebanese immigrants in Brooklyn
  • Ukrainian refugees on Long Island

This means an applicant can demonstrate an international journalism perspective through reporting conducted domestically, provided the work engages meaningfully with international communities or issues.

Scholar Awards Reception and Professional Development

Award recipients will participate in a Scholar Awards reception in New York City in March 2027.

The event will form part of a two-day series of events involving:

  • Relevant training
  • Networking
  • Professional journalists

Winners are required to participate in the event.

This provides recipients with an opportunity to connect with other journalists and professionals while participating in activities related to their development as international journalists.

Join a Community of International Journalists

The opportunity extends beyond the financial award.

Recipients become part of a longstanding community of:

  • International journalists
  • Previous Scholar Award recipients
  • Journalism professionals

According to the Foundation, this network provides opportunities to:

  • Build professional connections
  • Exchange ideas
  • Stay connected with other journalists throughout their careers

For students beginning careers in international journalism, this community can form part of their longer-term professional network.

Examples From Previous Scholar Award Recipients

The Foundation highlights experiences from previous recipients to demonstrate how the awards have supported journalism careers.

Youcef Bounab

Youcef Bounab attended the Craig Newmark School of Journalism at CUNY.

His award included a Harper’s Magazine Scholarship and an OPC Foundation Fellowship with the Associated Press in Paris.

According to his account, the fellowship gave him the opportunity to report from Paris and work on a wide range of stories, including interviews with government officials, the head of the Paris Olympic committee, booksellers, and others. He later became a Maghreb correspondent for Agence France-Presse, based in Tunisia and covering much of North Africa.

Catherine Cartier

Catherine Cartier attended New York University and received the Reuters Scholarship 2024 with an OPC Foundation Fellowship with Reuters in Dubai.

Her fellowship involved reporting on:

  • Finance
  • Energy
  • Breaking news

She also interviewed people from different sectors and reported on developments in the Gulf region. According to her account, the experience influenced her subsequent international reporting.

Brunella Tipismana

Brunella Tipismana attended Yale University and received the Seymour and Audrey Topping Scholarship in 2024.

The Foundation includes her among its previous Scholar Award recipients.

Brett Simpson

Brett Simpson attended the University of California-Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism and received the Irene Corbally Kuhn Scholarship in 2021.

According to his account, the scholarship supported reporting in the Norwegian Arctic concerning an Indigenous rights protest related to a state-sanctioned copper mine on Sámi reindeer-herding lands.

The resulting reporting appeared in National Geographic in 2022, and he described the experience as influential in shaping his subsequent reporting career focused on climate, energy, and human rights.

Stephen Kalin

Stephen Kalin attended the American University in Cairo and received the Roy Rowan Scholarship in 2013.

He described using the scholarship to support a summer internship with Reuters, beginning in Lebanon and subsequently working on assignments in Egypt, Iraq, and Saudi Arabia.

His account describes the early support as influential in his subsequent career in foreign reporting.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Although the Foundation provides specific requirements rather than a step-by-step preparation strategy, applicants can organize their preparation around the stated criteria.

1. Choose a clear international journalism focus

Identify the international region, community, issue, or subject area that genuinely connects with your journalism interests.

2. Select your strongest work sample

Choose one format:

  • Print
  • Photo
  • Video
  • Audio

The selected work should demonstrate your journalism abilities and connect with your international interests.

3. Follow the format requirements exactly

For example:

  • Print: 600–800 words
  • Photojournalism: photographs plus approximately 500 words of context
  • Video/audio: 2–7 minutes plus approximately 500 words of context

4. Make your role clear

For collaborative journalism, explain your specific contribution and properly credit other members of the team.

5. Keep your application focused

The Foundation warns that exceedingly long applications may be disqualified. Follow the requested length requirements and avoid unnecessary material.

6. Proofread carefully

The Foundation specifically advises applicants to carefully proofread their materials.

7. Address AI use appropriately

If AI was used in preparing any application material, follow the Foundation’s requirement that responsible AI use be clearly disclosed.

Important Dates

Date Event
November 15, 2026 Application deadline
Mid-January 2027 Winners expected to be contacted and posted on the Foundation’s website
March 2027 Scholar Awards reception and two-day training/networking event in New York City

The Foundation states that winners will be contacted by mid-January and posted on its website.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Award?

It is a student-focused journalism award program that provides financial support to students pursuing international journalism, with awards generally taking the form of scholarships or fellowships.

How many awards are normally offered?

In a typical year, the Foundation grants 18 Scholar Awards.

How much funding can recipients receive?

Recipients receive either a $3,000 scholarship or a $4,000 fellowship, depending on the award.

Do I need to have traveled internationally?

No. The Foundation explicitly states that applicants do not need to have traveled abroad to apply.

Can my work focus on an international community in the United States?

Yes. Previous examples cited by the Foundation include reporting on Syrian and Lebanese immigrants in Brooklyn and Ukrainian refugees on Long Island.

Can graduate students apply?

Yes. College juniors, college seniors, and graduate students enrolled in a degree program at the application deadline are identified as eligible applicant categories.

What file formats are accepted?

The complete application must be submitted as one document, using either .docx or .pdf, with a maximum size of 10 MB.

What language must the application be in?

Application materials must be submitted in English. Work originally produced in another language must be accompanied by an English translation.

When is the deadline?

The application deadline is Sunday, November 15, 2026.

Conclusion

The Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards 2027 provide an opportunity for university students interested in international journalism to receive financial support while developing their journalism careers.

The program typically offers 18 awards, with recipients receiving either a $3,000 scholarship or a $4,000 fellowship. The fellowship option can support time in the bureau of a major news organization, while the scholarship option can support independent work.

Applicants can come from a variety of national backgrounds, but they must meet the program’s specific enrollment requirements. Eligible pathways include international students studying at U.S. colleges or universities and U.S. citizens studying abroad.

The application requires a one-page cover letter, one-page resume, and a journalism work sample in print, photography, video, or audio. Applicants should pay close attention to the specified requirements for their selected format and ensure that their work demonstrates strong journalism and international relevance.

The deadline is November 15, 2026, making early preparation particularly important for students who need to develop or reformat their journalism samples.

Apply through the official Overseas Press Club Foundation submission page

For more opportunities here

item.content:encoded:
The University of Leeds is offering a highly competitive ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship for postgraduate researchers interested in the changing relationship between digital technologies, artificial intelligence, skills, employment, regional economies and the future of work.

The scholarship is based at Leeds University Business School and forms part of the ESRC Research Centre for Digital Futures at Work (Digit), a major research centre focused on understanding how digital transformation is reshaping work, employment and society.

For the 2026/27 academic cycle, the opportunity provides full academic fees together with a tax-free maintenance grant currently valued at £21,805 per year, with the maintenance amount increasing annually in line with UKRI rates. The funding is available for a period of up to 3.5 years for full-time study, making this a significant doctoral funding opportunity for applicants whose research interests align with the advertised project.

The application deadline is 31 October 2026, with the scholarship scheduled to begin on 1 February 2027. There is one funding place available.

About the ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship

The scholarship is attached to a specific doctoral research project titled:

“Building good work and digital skills within a regional digital eco-system.”

The proposed research examines how local authorities and regional agencies can develop inclusive digital and skills ecosystems within regional labour markets.

The project is particularly concerned with how regional economies respond to technological and economic restructuring and how institutions can support:

  • Digital skills readiness
  • Digital transformation within regional economies
  • Adoption of artificial intelligence and digital technologies
  • Digital skills upgrading
  • Sustainable employment
  • Good work
  • Inclusive regional development
  • Institutional capacity for supporting technological change

The research will be situated within the United Kingdom’s broader strategy for digital adoption and economic growth.

The studentship will use both qualitative and, where appropriate, quantitative research methods. It is expected to involve interviews with important actors such as local policymakers, employers and workers. The successful doctoral researcher will also collaborate with key local actors and undertake an internship connected to the research project.

University of Leeds Research Environment

The scholarship is located within the ESRC Research Centre for Digital Futures at Work (Digit) and based at Leeds University Business School.

Digit is a multi-institutional research centre established in 2020 and led from the Universities of Leeds and Sussex. According to the University of Leeds, the centre has received £18 million in funding from the ESRC and provides a research environment for doctoral students and early-career researchers.

Successful students will have access to Digit’s doctoral and early-career researcher networks, alongside additional support for areas such as:

  • Research consumables
  • Training
  • Conference attendance
  • Doctoral and early-career research networks
  • Research collaboration
  • The wider research facilities of Leeds University Business School

Leeds University Business School also houses a large academic department specialising in work and employment research through its People, Work and Employment Department.

Scholarship Funding and Financial Support

The ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship provides substantial financial support for doctoral study.

For full-time study, the award includes:

  • Full academic fees
  • Maintenance grant of £21,805 for the 2026/27 session
  • Annual increases to the maintenance grant in line with the UKRI rate
  • Maintenance support for 3.5 years
  • Full fee coverage for 3 years

Part-time awards are provided on a pro-rata basis.

Research Focus: Digital Futures at Work

The central research theme of the scholarship is the relationship between digital transformation, skills and employment.

The doctoral project provides an opportunity to investigate how regional labour markets can adapt to rapid technological change while ensuring that workers and communities can benefit from emerging opportunities.

Potential research questions within the broad project could relate to issues such as:

  1. How regional economies prepare for digital transformation.
  2. How governments and regional institutions can improve digital skills readiness.
  3. How artificial intelligence adoption affects regional labour markets.
  4. How workers can acquire new digital skills as industries change.
  5. How employers can support digital skills development.
  6. How regional institutions can promote sustainable employment.
  7. How technological change can be connected to the creation of good work.
  8. How policymakers can develop inclusive digital ecosystems.
  9. How local employers and workers experience digital transformation.
  10. How institutional capacity influences the adoption of emerging technologies.

Applicants are not restricted to simply repeating the wording of the advertised project. The University states that applicants can pursue their own research interests within the broad area specified in the scholarship advertisement.

Conclusion

The ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship at the University of Leeds provides an opportunity for doctoral researchers to investigate how digital technologies, artificial intelligence, skills development and changing labour markets are shaping the future of work.

The scholarship combines substantial financial support with access to a specialist research environment through the ESRC Research Centre for Digital Futures at Work and Leeds University Business School. The proposed research focuses specifically on building good work and digital skills within regional digital ecosystems, while allowing the successful researcher to develop their own research interests within the broader theme.

With full academic fees, a £21,805 maintenance grant for 2026/27, research and training support, and funding for up to 3.5 years of full-time study, the opportunity is designed for strong doctoral candidates whose academic and research interests align with digital futures, skills, employment and regional economic transformation.

Prospective applicants should begin the process early because they must first secure a research study application and prepare the required supporting documentation. The final scholarship deadline is 31 October 2026, and the award is scheduled to commence on 1 February 2027.

Applicants should ensure that their academic qualifications, proposed research, supporting documents and English-language evidence meet the stated requirements before submitting their application.
